title: Advanced II (Word Smart–style)
description: GRE-level words with original learner definitions. Import your own Word Smart 2 list in Settings to add the book's words.

words.definition: to make something bad less serious or harmful
examples: Planting trees can *mitigate* the effects of pollution.
Nothing could *mitigate* her disappointment.

words.definition: evil or criminal
examples: The villain had a *nefarious* plan to steal the jewels.
They were involved in *nefarious* activities.

words.definition: too eager to please or obey someone important
examples: The *obsequious* assistant agreed with everything his boss said.
I can't stand his *obsequious* flattery.

words.definition: not well known or hard to understand; (verb) to hide from view
examples: The poem is full of *obscure* references.
Clouds *obscured* the moon.

words.definition: too concerned with small details or rules, often to show off knowledge
examples: His *pedantic* comments about grammar annoyed everyone.
Don't be *pedantic* — we understand what she meant.

words.definition: dealing with problems in a practical, realistic way
examples: We need a *pragmatic* solution, not a perfect one.
She took a *pragmatic* approach to saving money.

words.definition: producing a lot of work or results
examples: Agatha Christie was a *prolific* writer.
Rabbits are *prolific* breeders.

words.definition: careful and wise, especially when thinking about the future
examples: It would be *prudent* to save some money.
A *prudent* investor doesn't take big risks.

words.definition: not willing to talk about your feelings or private matters
examples: He was *reticent* about his past.
She is *reticent* in large groups.

words.definition: hopeful and confident about the future
examples: She is *sanguine* about her chances of winning.
Investors are less *sanguine* this year.

words.definition: very careful to be honest and do what is right; very careful about details
examples: A *scrupulous* accountant checks every number.
He was *scrupulous* about telling the truth.

words.definition: false, although it may seem to be true
examples: The article made *spurious* claims about the medicine.
Don't trust *spurious* statistics.

words.definition: not giving up easily; holding something firmly
examples: She is a *tenacious* reporter who always finds the truth.
The baby had a *tenacious* grip on my finger.

words.definition: seeming to be everywhere at the same time
examples: Smartphones are now *ubiquitous*.
Coffee shops are *ubiquitous* in Seoul.

words.definition: to respect someone or something very deeply
examples: Many cultures *venerate* their ancestors.
The old professor was *venerated* by his students.

words.definition: using more words than are needed
examples: His *verbose* report could be half as long.
Avoid *verbose* sentences in your essay.

words.definition: to prove that someone is right or not guilty
examples: The new evidence *vindicated* the prisoner.
Her decision was *vindicated* by the results.

words.definition: showing great energy and enthusiasm for a belief or goal
examples: He is a *zealous* supporter of animal rights.
The *zealous* new employee worked late every night.

words.definition: a person or thing that is mysterious and hard to understand
examples: The ancient stone circle remains an *enigma*.
Even to her friends, she was an *enigma*.

words.definition: understood by only a small group of people with special knowledge
examples: The professor's lecture was too *esoteric* for most students.
He collects *esoteric* facts about old maps.

words.definition: to make a bad situation worse
examples: Scratching will only *exacerbate* the itch.
The drought *exacerbated* the food shortage.

words.definition: very careful about details, cleanliness or correctness
examples: He is *fastidious* about keeping his desk clean.
The chef is *fastidious* about fresh ingredients.

words.definition: done without a good reason; unnecessary
examples: The movie had too much *gratuitous* violence.
That was a *gratuitous* insult.

words.definition: lazy; not wanting to work or be active
examples: The *indolent* cat slept all afternoon in the sun.
He was criticized for his *indolent* attitude.

words.definition: not harmful or offensive
examples: It was an *innocuous* question, but she got angry.
Most spiders are *innocuous* to humans.

words.definition: having little taste or interest; boring
examples: The soup was *insipid* and needed salt.
The movie had an *insipid* plot.

words.definition: using very few words
examples: His *laconic* reply was just "No."
The *laconic* cowboy rarely spoke.

words.definition: talking a lot
examples: Our *loquacious* taxi driver told us his whole life story.
She becomes *loquacious* when she's nervous.

words.definition: generous and kind, especially toward a rival or someone weaker
examples: The *magnanimous* winner praised her opponent.
It was *magnanimous* of him to forgive them.

words.definition: showing off wealth or importance to impress people
examples: They live in an *ostentatious* mansion with gold doors.
He wore an *ostentatious* watch.
